summary: Goochland County tower point the FFLA marks gone and a FOREST LOOKOUTS page calls removed; no build date found, and the standing Rassawek tower is not tied to it.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association marks the Gum Spring point gone. The FOREST LOOKOUTS page marks it removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA marks the Gum Spring point gone and the FOREST LOOKOUTS page marks it removed. Both mean the tower is no longer there, so the record keeps gone. The page does not give a date.

notes_for_editor: Three register-free sources, each a stub: the FFLA lists give coordinates and gone only; the FOREST LOOKOUTS page gives county and removed only. No build date, design, height, builder, agency, staffing, fires, access or visit detail in any source read. The FFLA says the standing Rassawek tower is relocated East Leake without saying which point, so it is not tied to Gum Spring here; see the existing us-va-east-leake-at-rassawek story. Unverified leads not used because they could not be read from cache: a Waymarking page (WM6Q0E) whose search snippet says a Goochland fire tower was relocated from Hanover County, which would conflict with the FFLA's relocated-East-Leake claim; and a Facebook group post whose snippet says East Leake stood on the south side of U.S. Route 250, about 100 feet off the road on private property. Check both before editing the Rassawek or East Leake stories.
